questions.q: The international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, known as the Ramsar Convention, was signed in which year?
questions.why: The convention was signed on February 2, 1971, in the Iranian city of Ramsar, establishing global wetland protection.

questions.q: In which year did the Ramsar Convention officially come into force in India?
questions.why: India formally became a contracting party to the Ramsar Convention on February 1, 1982, adopting international conservation standards.

questions.q: Following the latest environmental updates in 2026, what is the total number of designated Ramsar sites in India?
questions.why: India's Ramsar network expanded to exactly 99 sites by mid-2026, marking it as the largest network in South Asia.

questions.q: Which wetland was officially designated as the 99th Ramsar site of India in May 2026?
questions.why: Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, was officially recognized as India's 99th Ramsar site in May 2026.

questions.q: Which two Indian cities were accredited as India's first ever Ramsar Wetland Cities in January 2025?
questions.why: Indore in Madhya Pradesh and Udaipur in Rajasthan received prestigious international accreditation as India's first Wetland Cities in January 2025.

questions.q: Which were the first two wetlands in India to be designated as Ramsar sites in 1981?
opts: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.ansText: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.why: Chilika Lake in Odisha and Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan were the first two Indian sites recognized in 1981.

questions.q: Which is the largest designated Ramsar site in India by total surface area?
questions.why: Sundarbans Wetland in West Bengal is the largest Ramsar site in India, covering over 4,000 square kilometers of mangrove ecosystems.

questions.q: Which is the smallest Ramsar site in India by total surface area?
questions.why: Renuka Wetland in Himachal Pradesh is the smallest Ramsar site in the country, spanning a surface area of just 20 hectares.

questions.q: Which Indian state holds the highest number of designated Ramsar sites as of 2026?
questions.why: Tamil Nadu comfortably leads the country with a remarkable 20 Ramsar sites, followed closely by Uttar Pradesh with 13.

questions.q: The recently added Chhari-Dhand conservation reserve Ramsar site is located in which state?
questions.why: Chhari-Dhand is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat and was formally added to the Ramsar list in early 2026.

questions.q: Which two Indian wetlands are currently listed under the global Montreux Record?
opts: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
Wular Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.ansText: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
questions.why: Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan and Loktak Lake in Manipur remain on the Montreux Record due to ecological shifts.

questions.q: Which Indian Ramsar site was successfully removed from the Montreux Record in 2002 after extensive environmental restoration?
questions.why: Chilika Lake in Odisha was removed from the Montreux Record in 2002 following highly successful rehabilitation and conservation efforts.

questions.q: Which wetland became Chhattisgarh's first ever designated Ramsar site in late 2025?
questions.why: Kopra Jalashay in Bilaspur was officially designated as Chhattisgarh's first ever Ramsar site in late 2025.

questions.q: Which wetland was designated as the first ever Ramsar site of Sikkim in 2025?
questions.why: Khachoedpalri Wetland was recognized as Sikkim's maiden Ramsar site in 2025 due to its immense hydrological and cultural importance.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in India is famous for floating biomass islands called 'Phumdis' and houses the Keibul Lamjao National Park?
questions.why: Loktak Lake in Manipur is world-famous for its unique floating islands called phumdis and the endangered sangai deer population.

questions.q: The Patna Bird Sanctuary, designated as a Ramsar site in early 2026, is located in which state?
questions.why: Despite its name, Patna Bird Sanctuary is located in the Etah district of Uttar Pradesh and was added in early 2026.

questions.q: World Wetlands Day is celebrated globally every year on which date?
questions.why: February 2 marks the date of adoption of the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands in the Iranian city of Ramsar in 1971.

questions.q: Where is the official international head office of the Secretariat of the Ramsar Convention located?
questions.why: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is centrally hosted at the global headquarters of the IUCN in Gland, Switzerland.

questions.q: Which country has the highest total number of designated Ramsar sites in the world?
questions.why: The United Kingdom leads the world with over 170 designated Ramsar sites within its territory.

questions.q: What is the global rank of India in terms of the total number of Ramsar sites as of mid-2026?
questions.why: India ranks 3rd globally by total number of sites, behind the United Kingdom and Mexico, and ranks first in Asia.

questions.q: The Nagi and Nakti Bird Sanctuaries, which were designated as Ramsar sites, are located in which state?
questions.why: Nagi and Nakti Bird Sanctuaries are located in the Jamui district of Bihar and were added to the list in recent years.

questions.q: Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary was added to the list of Ramsar sites in 2025. It is located in which state?
questions.why: Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary is located in the Sahibganj district of Jharkhand, serving as a critical habitat for migratory birds.

questions.q: Which India-led resolution was successfully adopted at the Ramsar CoP-15 held in July 2025?
opts: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands
questions.ansText: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands
questions.why: India successfully spearheaded this global resolution at CoP-15, aligning completely with its lifestyle-focused Mission LiFE initiative.

questions.q: Tawa Reservoir, declared as a prominent Ramsar site, is located in which state?
questions.why: Tawa Reservoir is a large artificial reservoir located in the Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh and was designated in 2024.

questions.q: Lonar Lake Ramsar site in Maharashtra is highly unique because it was formed by which natural process?
questions.why: Lonar Lake is a high-velocity basaltic rock impact crater lake formed by a meteorite during the Pleistocene Epoch.

questions.q: Deepor Beel, the only designated Ramsar site of its state, is located in:
questions.why: Deepor Beel is a large permanent freshwater lake located southwest of Guwahati in Assam, critical for conservation.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site is globally renowned for being a natural, low-cost urban sewage treatment system for a major metro city?
questions.why: The East Kolkata Wetlands treat urban sewage for Kolkata through a combination of aquaculture, recycling, and agriculture.

questions.q: Kabartal Wetland, also known as Kanwar Jheel, is Asia's largest oxbow lake. In which state is it located?
questions.why: Kabartal is located in the Begusarai district of Bihar and serves as a major freshwater oxbow wetland habitat.

questions.q: Pala Wetland, the largest natural wetland in its state, is located in:
questions.why: Pala Wetland is located in the Saiha district of Mizoram and is highly vital for local tribal livelihoods and bio-diversity.

questions.q: The wetlands of Khichan and Menar, added to the Ramsar list in 2025, are situated in which state?
questions.why: Khichan (world-famous for Demoiselle Cranes) and Menar (known as the bird village) are both located in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary Ramsar site is located along the banks of which major river?
questions.why: Ranganathittu is a premier bird sanctuary located on small islets within the Kaveri River in Karnataka.

questions.q: Sakhya Sagar lake Ramsar site is located inside which prominent National Park?
questions.why: Sakhya Sagar is situated within the boundaries of the Madhav National Park in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Haiderpur Wetland, a massive human-made wetland designated as a Ramsar site, is located in which state?
questions.why: Haiderpur Wetland was formed following the construction of the Madhya Ganga Barrage in western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Bhoj Wetland consists of two lakes, the Upper Lake and Lower Lake, located in which major city?
questions.why: Bhoj Wetland is located in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, and provides crucial ecological benefits and drinking water to the city.

questions.q: Ashtamudi and Sasthamkotta lakes are prominent Ramsar sites located in which Indian state?
questions.why: Both Ashtamudi (a massive estuary) and Sasthamkotta (a freshwater lake) are situated in Kerala.

questions.q: Nanda Lake, designated as a prominent Ramsar site, is the first and only Ramsar site of which state?
questions.why: Nanda Lake is located in Curchorem, Goa, and stands as a vital freshwater marsh ecosystem for the state.

questions.q: Harike Wetland in Punjab was formed by constructing a barrage at the confluence of which two major rivers?
questions.why: Harike is a man-made riverine wetland located at the immediate confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers in Punjab.

questions.q: Rudrasagar Lake, featuring the famous water palace 'Neermahal', is a Ramsar site located in which state?
questions.why: Rudrasagar Lake is a natural sedimentation reservoir located in Melaghar, Tripura.

questions.q: Sambhar Lake, India's largest inland salt lake and a designated Ramsar site, is primarily commercially famous for:
questions.why: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan produces a major portion of India's commercial salt using brine extraction.

questions.q: Wular Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia and a Ramsar site, is fed primarily by which river?
questions.why: Wular Lake is located in Jammu and Kashmir and is naturally fed and drained by the path of the Jhelum River.

questions.q: Sultanpur National Park Ramsar site is situated in which district of Haryana?
questions.why: Sultanpur National Park is located on the Gurugram-Jhajjar highway in the state of Haryana.

questions.q: Thol Lake Wildlife Sanctuary is a shallow freshwater Ramsar site situated in which state?
questions.why: Thol Lake is an artificial wetland and wildlife sanctuary located in the Mehsana district of Gujarat.

questions.q: Keoladeo National Park, one of India's very first Ramsar sites, was historically known by which name?
questions.why: Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan was formerly known as the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary before its status upgrade.

questions.q: Kolleru Lake, a major freshwater Ramsar site, lies between the deltas of which two major rivers?
questions.why: Kolleru Lake is located in Andhra Pradesh, nesting securely between the Godavari and Krishna river basins.

questions.q: Bakhira Wildlife Sanctuary, the largest natural floodplain wetland of Eastern UP, was added to the Ramsar list in:
questions.why: Bakhira Wildlife Sanctuary in Sant Kabir Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, was officially designated as a Ramsar site in late 2021.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Odisha is renowned for hosting the largest population of saltwater crocodiles in India?
questions.why: Bhitarkanika is a massive mangrove ecosystem in Odisha, world-famous for its saltwater crocodiles and Olive Ridley turtles.

questions.q: The Tso Kar wetland complex, added as a Ramsar site, is located in which region of India?
questions.why: Tso Kar, meaning 'White Lake', is a highly saline lake in the Changthang region of Ladakh known for its white salt efflorescence.

questions.q: Which is the first and only Ramsar site of Uttarakhand, located at the confluence of the Yamuna and Asan rivers?
questions.why: Asan Conservation Reserve was declared Uttarakhand's first Ramsar site in 2020, serving as a critical habitat for migratory birds.

questions.q: Nandur Madhmeshwar, often called the 'Bharatpur of Maharashtra', is located on which river?
questions.why: It is Maharashtra's first Ramsar site, formed by a dam built across the Godavari River in the Nashik district.

questions.q: The Beas Conservation Reserve in Punjab is the only known habitat in India for which endangered freshwater mammal?
questions.why: The Beas Conservation Reserve hosts the only isolated population of the endangered Indus River Dolphin in India.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Himachal Pradesh is known as the 'Maharana Pratap Sagar'?
questions.why: Created in 1975 by building an earthfill dam on the Beas River, it was named Maharana Pratap Sagar and is a major Ramsar site.

questions.q: Bhindawas Wildlife Sanctuary, designated as a Ramsar site, is the largest human-made freshwater wetland in which state?
questions.why: Bhindawas is an important ecological corridor and the largest artificial freshwater wetland in Haryana.

questions.q: The Central Government launched which scheme in the 2023-24 Budget to promote the unique conservation values of Ramsar Sites?
questions.why: Amrit Dharohar is a dedicated scheme launched for a period of three years to encourage optimal use of wetlands and enhance eco-tourism.

questions.q: Under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules of 2017, who is the nodal authority for wetland management at the state level?
questions.why: The 2017 rules decentralized wetland management, creating State Wetland Authorities headed by the respective State Environment Ministers.

questions.q: Which state is home to the high-altitude oligotrophic lake Ramsar site known as Tso Moriri?
questions.why: Tso Moriri is a pristine high-altitude lake in the Changthang plateau of Ladakh, designated as a Ramsar site in 2002.

questions.q: Satkosia Gorge, a designated Ramsar site, is a deep gorge carved by which major Indian river?
questions.why: Satkosia Gorge in Odisha was carved by the Mahanadi River and is an important habitat for the endangered gharial.

questions.q: Thane Creek, which was added to the Ramsar list, is globally renowned for hosting tens of thousands of which bird species?
questions.why: Thane Creek in Maharashtra is highly famous for its massive seasonal congregation of Greater and Lesser Flamingos.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Gujarat is the largest natural freshwater lake in the state?
questions.why: Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary is the largest natural wetland in Gujarat, added to the Ramsar list in 2012.

questions.q: The Ansupa Lake Ramsar site is an oxbow lake formed by the meandering of the Mahanadi river in which state?
questions.why: Ansupa is a prominent freshwater oxbow lake situated on the left bank of the Mahanadi river in Odisha.

questions.q: Surinsar-Mansar Lakes, designated as a Ramsar site, are located in which Indian Union Territory?
questions.why: These twin lakes in Jammu and Kashmir are heavily tied to Hindu mythology (Mahabharata) and hold immense ecological value.

questions.q: Kanjli Wetland, a man-made Ramsar site in Punjab, was created by building a barrage across which rivulet?
questions.why: Kanjli was formed in 1870 by constructing a barrage across the Kali Bein rivulet, a tributary of the Beas River.

questions.q: The Ropar Wetland in Punjab is a man-made freshwater riverine and lacustrine wetland located on which river?
questions.why: Ropar Wetland was created by a barrage built on the Sutlej River and is a critical staging ground for migratory birds.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Uttar Pradesh was formerly known as Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary before being renamed?
opts: Shahid Chandra Shekhar Azad Bird Sanctuary
questions.ansText: Shahid Chandra Shekhar Azad Bird Sanctuary
questions.why: The Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary in Unnao was renamed in 2015 to honor the freedom fighter Chandra Shekhar Azad.

questions.q: Parvati Arga Bird Sanctuary, a designated Ramsar site comprising two oxbow lakes, is located in which state?
questions.why: Parvati Arga is located in the Gonda district of Uttar Pradesh and provides a vital wintering site for migratory waterbirds.

questions.q: Sarsai Nawar Jheel, a Ramsar site in Uttar Pradesh, is particularly famous for conserving which large bird species?
questions.why: Located in the Etawah district, Sarsai Nawar is a typical Indo-Gangetic floodplain wetland known for its resident Sarus Cranes.

questions.q: Sur Sarovar Ramsar site, also known as Keetham Lake, is situated alongside the Yamuna river in which city?
questions.why: Sur Sarovar (Keetham Lake) is a scenic human-made wetland located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, added to the Ramsar list in 2020.

questions.q: The Upper Ganga River stretch, which is a designated Ramsar site, extends between which two locations?
questions.why: This 85 km stretch of the Ganges from Brijghat to Narora in UP is a Ramsar site protecting the Ganges river dolphin and gharials.

questions.q: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar site featuring dry evergreen forests and mangroves, is in:
questions.why: Located on the Coromandel Coast in Tamil Nadu, it was one of the earliest Ramsar sites designated in southern India.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Tamil Nadu is the second largest mangrove forest in the world after the Sundarbans?
questions.why: Pichavaram in Tamil Nadu is a vast estuarine mangrove forest and one of the largest such ecosystems on the planet.

questions.q: The Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve Ramsar site is critical for the conservation of which marine mammal?
questions.why: The Gulf of Mannar in Tamil Nadu is India's first marine biosphere reserve, famous for its population of the endangered Dugong (sea cow).

questions.q: Pallikaranai Marsh Reserve Forest, one of the last remaining natural wetlands of its kind, is located in which major city?
questions.why: Pallikaranai is a freshwater marsh in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, playing a crucial role in flood mitigation for the metropolis.

questions.q: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar site in Tamil Nadu, is historically significant because it is:
opts: The oldest water bird sanctuary in India
The only habitat of the spot-billed pelican
questions.ansText: The oldest water bird sanctuary in India
questions.why: Vedanthangal is the oldest water bird sanctuary in India, protected by the local community for over 250 years.

questions.q: Longwood Shola Reserve Forest, designated as a Ramsar site, is a fragile tropical montane forest located in:
questions.why: Longwood Shola is a highly localized, high-altitude Shola forest ecosystem near Kotagiri in the Nilgiris of Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Madhya Pradesh was formed by creating a barrage across the Gambhir River?
questions.why: Yashwant Sagar is a reservoir in Indore, MP, created on the Gambhir river and is an Important Bird Area (IBA) for the Sarus Crane.

questions.q: Khijadia Wildlife Sanctuary, a unique Ramsar site featuring both fresh water and salt water habitats, is in:
questions.why: Located near Jamnagar in Gujarat, Khijadia has reclamation bunds that uniquely separate fresh water from sea water.

questions.q: Aghanashini Estuary, added to the Ramsar list, is known for traditional integrated farming systems. Where is it located?
questions.why: The Aghanashini Estuary in Karnataka is a free-flowing river estuary completely free of dams, highly vital for local biodiversity.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Karnataka is a human-made tank that hosts thousands of wintering Bar-headed Geese?
questions.why: Magadi Kere is a wetland in the Gadag district of Karnataka, serving as one of the largest wintering grounds for the Bar-headed Goose.

questions.q: Hokera Wetland, designated as a Ramsar site, acts as a major staging ground for birds migrating via the Central Asian Flyway. It is located in:
questions.why: Hokera (or Hokersar) is an important wetland in the Kashmir Valley, situated in the Jhelum river basin just outside Srinagar.

questions.q: The Keshopur-Miani Community Reserve Ramsar site is unique because it is India's first ever:
questions.why: Located in Punjab, Keshopur-Miani was the first notified community reserve in India, managed jointly by the forest department and locals.

questions.q: Chandertal Wetland in Himachal Pradesh is a high-altitude Ramsar site located in the upper reaches of which river valley?
questions.why: Chandertal (Lake of the Moon) is a sweet water lake situated at an altitude of about 4,300 meters in the Lahaul and Spiti district.

questions.q: Vellode Bird Sanctuary, an important Ramsar site in Tamil Nadu, is located in which district?
questions.why: Vellode Bird Sanctuary is a large artificial tank located in the Erode district, functioning as an essential habitat for resident and migratory birds.

questions.q: Which wetland in Tamil Nadu is an ancient irrigation tank that also serves as a prominent Ramsar site?
questions.why: Vaduvur is a large, human-made irrigation tank and bird sanctuary located in the Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Odisha is the longest earthen dam in the world?
questions.why: Built across the Mahanadi River, the Hirakud Reservoir is the longest earthen dam globally and a highly critical aquatic ecosystem.

questions.q: Which of the following Ramsar sites in Uttar Pradesh is located in the Hardoi district?
questions.why: Sandi Bird Sanctuary is a freshwater marsh in the Hardoi district, providing a vital wintering area for diverse waterfowl.

questions.q: The Samaspur Bird Sanctuary Ramsar site is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.why: Samaspur is a perennial lowland marsh situated in the Rae Bareli district, established as a sanctuary in 1987.

questions.q: Which state is home to the Tampara Lake Ramsar site, a prominent freshwater lake situated near the Rushikulya river?
questions.why: Tampara Lake is a sweet water depression in the Ganjam district of Odisha, playing a key role in regional hydrology.

questions.q: Ankasamudra Bird Conservation Reserve, a human-made village irrigation tank and Ramsar site, is in:
questions.why: Ankasamudra is an ecologically significant wetland situated in the Vijayanagara district of Karnataka.

questions.q: Wadhvana Wetland, an internationally important wintering ground for waterbirds, is a Ramsar site located near which city?
questions.why: Wadhvana is a century-old reservoir located in the Vadodara district of Gujarat, known for attracting immense flocks of migratory birds.

questions.q: The Ramsar Convention defines wetlands to include areas of marine water the depth of which at low tide does not exceed:
questions.why: Under Article 1 of the convention, wetlands include marine areas where the low-tide depth does not exceed six meters.

questions.q: Hygam Wetland Conservation Reserve, which was heavily silted but successfully restored as a Ramsar site, is in:
questions.why: Hygam is a shallow reed-bed wetland in the Baramulla district of J&K, vital for flood absorption in the Jhelum basin.

questions.q: Shallbugh Wetland Conservation Reserve, heavily dependent on snowmelt water, is a Ramsar site in:
questions.why: Shallbugh is a vast riverine marsh in the Ganderbal district of J&K, providing vital habitat for migratory species.

questions.q: Nangal Wildlife Sanctuary, designated as a Ramsar site, is located in the Shivalik foothills of which state?
questions.why: Nangal Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Rupnagar district of Punjab, surrounding the Bhakra-Nangal dam infrastructure.

questions.q: Udhayamarthandapuram Bird Sanctuary is a protected Ramsar site situated in which state?
questions.why: It is an important irrigation tank turned bird sanctuary located in the Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Chitrangudi Bird Sanctuary, also locally known as 'Pelicanry', is a Ramsar site in:
questions.why: Located in the Ramanathapuram district of Tamil Nadu, Chitrangudi is highly noted for its nesting colonies of Spot-billed Pelicans.

questions.q: Which state hosts the Suchindram Theroor Wetland Complex, a Ramsar site forming part of the active flyway network?
questions.why: This complex is situated in the Kanyakumari district of Tamil Nadu and is an important component of the Central Asian Flyway.

questions.q: Kanjirankulam Bird Sanctuary, known for nesting Painted Storks and Egrets, is a Ramsar site located in:
questions.why: Kanjirankulam is located in the Ramanathapuram district of Tamil Nadu and is a prime breeding ground for colonial waterbirds.

questions.q: Karaivetti Bird Sanctuary, a designated Ramsar site that stores agricultural water, is located in which district?
questions.why: Karaivetti is an essential freshwater lake in the Ariyalur district of Tamil Nadu, acting as a major water source and bird habitat.

questions.q: Vembannur Wetland Complex is an artificial irrigation tank and Ramsar site in which state?
questions.why: Vembannur is an important, human-made irrigation tank ecosystem located in the Kanyakumari district of Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Saman Bird Sanctuary, an oxbow lake and Ramsar site, is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.why: Saman Bird Sanctuary is a seasonal oxbow lake situated in the Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh on the Ganges floodplain.

questions.q: Which of these organizations is NOT one of the six official International Organization Partners (IOPs) of the Ramsar Convention?
questions.why: Greenpeace is not an official IOP. The partners include IUCN, BirdLife International, WWF, Wetlands International, WWT, and IWMI.

questions.q: The 'Montreux Record' under the Ramsar Convention is primarily a register of:
opts: Wetlands where ecological character has degraded or is threatened
Wetlands that have been completely destroyed
questions.ansText: Wetlands where ecological character has degraded or is threatened
questions.why: The Montreux Record highlights sites in need of priority conservation attention due to human-induced ecological threats.

questions.q: Under the Ramsar Convention, the concept of 'Wise Use' of wetlands fundamentally aligns with which modern ecological principle?
questions.why: 'Wise Use' is defined as the maintenance of their ecological character, achieved through the implementation of sustainable development approaches.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in India was the very first to be placed on the Montreux Record in 1990?
questions.why: Keoladeo National Park was added to the Montreux Record in 1990 due to water shortages and unbalanced grazing negatively affecting the habitat.

questions.q: In which year were the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules strictly notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, replacing the older 2010 rules?
questions.why: The comprehensive 2017 rules decentralized wetland management, giving primary regulatory power back to state governments.

questions.q: The 'National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Eco-systems' (NPCA) was formed in 2013 by merging the National Lake Conservation Plan with the:
questions.why: The NPCA merged the lake and wetland conservation programs to create a unified framework for aquatic ecosystem health.

questions.q: As per Ramsar site designation criteria, a wetland is considered internationally important if it regularly supports what percentage of the individuals in a population of one species of waterbird?
questions.why: Criterion 6 of the Ramsar Convention states a wetland is internationally important if it regularly supports 1% of a species' global or regional population.

questions.q: Ramsar COP-14, which took place in 2022, was co-hosted by Geneva (Switzerland) and which other global city?
questions.why: COP-14 was uniquely co-hosted by Wuhan (China) and Geneva (Switzerland) due to pandemic-related logistical shifts.

questions.q: Which scheme was launched by the Indian government to specifically focus on the optimal utilization of Ramsar sites for local community empowerment?
questions.why: Amrit Dharohar aims to promote eco-tourism and sustainable livelihoods for local communities living around Ramsar sites.

questions.q: Alongside 'Amrit Dharohar', the 2023 Union Budget launched which specific scheme for the protection of Mangrove ecosystems in India?
questions.why: MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) was launched simultaneously to focus strictly on mangrove afforestation.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution indirectly mandates the protection of wetlands by stating it is the fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment?
questions.why: Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty to protect and improve lakes, rivers, forests, and wildlife.

questions.q: Which state Ramsar site is known for having a significant population of the critically endangered Gharial?
questions.why: Satkosia Gorge in Odisha on the Mahanadi River is a vital conservation area for the critically endangered Gharial crocodile.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Kerala is a massive estuary and acts as the gateway to the famous Kerala backwaters?
questions.why: Ashtamudi Wetland is a deep estuary in Kollam district, Kerala, possessing a unique palm-shaped topography and forming the entrance to the backwaters.

questions.q: Sasthamkotta Lake, a prominent Ramsar site, holds the distinction of being the largest freshwater lake in which state?
questions.why: Sasthamkotta Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Kerala, known for the absence of common aquatic plants due to the presence of a specific larva.

questions.q: The Vembanad-Kol Wetland Ramsar site is the longest lake in India and spans across several districts in which state?
questions.why: Vembanad-Kol is the longest lake in India and the largest Ramsar site in Kerala, playing a critical role in the region's hydrology and agriculture.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in India is an artificial reservoir created on the Beas River and is named after a famous Rajput king?
questions.why: Pong Dam Lake, designated as a Ramsar site, is officially named Maharana Pratap Sagar to honor the legendary Rajput warrior.

questions.q: Which of the following Ramsar sites is a high-altitude lake in the Lahaul and Spiti district, heavily associated with local folklore?
questions.why: Chandertal (Lake of the Moon) is a highly sacred and ecologically fragile wetland located in the Himalayas of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Renuka Lake Ramsar site in Himachal Pradesh is named after the mother of which mythological Hindu sage?
questions.why: The lake is named after Goddess Renuka, the mother of Lord Parashurama, and is shaped like the profile of a reclining woman.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Madhya Pradesh was historically created by Parmar King Raja Bhoj in the 11th century?
questions.why: Bhoj Wetland in Bhopal consists of the Upper Lake, which was created in the 11th century by the legendary King Bhoj.

questions.q: Sirpur Wetland, a major Ramsar site and Important Bird Area (IBA), is an ancient human-made lake located in:
questions.why: Sirpur Wetland was created by the Holkars in the 20th century in Indore and remains a critical urban wetland ecosystem.

questions.q: Which wetland in Odisha, designated as a Ramsar site, is a large freshwater oxbow lake famous for its scenic beauty and eco-tourism?
questions.why: Ansupa is a horseshoe-shaped freshwater oxbow lake in Cuttack, Odisha, formed by the Mahanadi River.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Jammu and Kashmir is deeply associated with the Mahabharata and the legend of Arjuna?
questions.why: Local legend dictates that Mansar Lake was created when Arjuna shot an arrow into the earth to extract water.

questions.q: Which is the only designated Ramsar site situated within the geographical boundaries of Tripura?
questions.why: Rudrasagar Lake in Tripura is the state's sole Ramsar site, famous for housing the stunning Neermahal water palace.

questions.q: Pala Wetland, the largest natural lake in Mizoram and a Ramsar site, is locally known by what name?
questions.why: In the local Mizo language, the Pala Wetland is called Palak Dil, representing a crucial biodiversity hotspot in the state.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Assam is a permanent freshwater lake and a major staging site for migratory birds traversing the East Asian-Australasian Flyway?
questions.why: Deepor Beel is Assam's only Ramsar site, functioning as an essential habitat for wild Asian elephants and migratory birds.

questions.q: Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan was added to the Montreux Record primarily due to problems related to:
opts: Water shortage and invasive weed species
questions.ansText: Water shortage and invasive weed species
questions.why: It was placed on the Montreux Record due to severe water shortages and the aggressive overgrowth of the invasive Paspalum distichum weed.

questions.q: Which specific weed's uncontrollable growth contributed to Loktak Lake being placed on the Montreux Record?
questions.why: The proliferation of water hyacinth (along with pollution and dam construction) severely impacted the Loktak Lake ecosystem.

questions.q: Chilika Lake was successfully removed from the Montreux Record in 2002 after clearing the blockage at its mouth connecting to the:
questions.why: Opening a new mouth to the Bay of Bengal restored the lake's salinity gradient, reviving the ecosystem and leading to its removal from the Montreux Record.

questions.q: The 'Ramsar Wetland City Accreditation' scheme was officially introduced during which COP meeting?
questions.why: The Wetland City Accreditation scheme was formally approved at COP-12 in Punta del Este, Uruguay, in 2015 to promote urban wetland conservation.

questions.q: Indore, which became one of India's first Ramsar Wetland Cities in 2025, boasts which two prominent Ramsar sites within its urban influence?
questions.why: Indore's accreditation as a Wetland City is heavily supported by the successful conservation of its two urban Ramsar sites: Sirpur and Yashwant Sagar.

questions.q: Udaipur, accredited alongside Indore as a Wetland City, is globally famous by what ecological nickname?
questions.why: Udaipur's intricate network of lakes (like Pichola and Fateh Sagar) earned it the title 'City of Lakes' and eventually the Wetland City Accreditation.

questions.q: Which state in India is entirely devoid of any designated Ramsar sites as of 2026?
questions.why: While almost all Indian states now have Ramsar sites (including Goa, Sikkim, and Jharkhand), Telangana currently has no designated Ramsar sites.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in West Bengal represents the only large-scale natural sewage treatment and resource recovery system in the world?
questions.why: The East Kolkata Wetlands uniquely treat the city's raw sewage through a complex, community-driven network of oxidation ponds and aquaculture.

questions.q: The Sundarbans Wetland Ramsar site is formed at the massive delta of which two major rivers?
questions.why: The Sundarbans, the largest Ramsar site in India, is a vast mangrove ecosystem situated at the confluence of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.q: Which Ramsar site in Bihar is recognized as the largest freshwater oxbow lake in the entire Asian continent?
questions.why: Kabartal Wetland (Kanwar Jheel) in Begusarai, Bihar, is formed by the meandering Gandak River and is Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake.

questions.q: Nagi and Nakti Bird Sanctuaries, both designated as Ramsar sites, were originally created primarily for what purpose?
questions.why: Both Nagi and Nakti are human-made reservoirs originally constructed to provide irrigation to the arid regions of Jamui, Bihar.

questions.q: The Khachoedpalri Wetland, Sikkim's first Ramsar site, is considered highly sacred by followers of which religion?
questions.why: Khachoedpalri Lake is considered a wish-fulfilling lake, heavily revered by both Buddhists and Hindus in the state of Sikkim.

questions.q: Kopra Jalashay, the inaugural Ramsar site of Chhattisgarh, serves as a crucial wintering ground for which Central Asian flyway species?
questions.why: Kopra Jalashay attracts massive flocks of Bar-headed Geese and other waterfowl migrating via the Central Asian Flyway.

questions.q: The Chhari-Dhand Wetland Conservation Reserve in Gujarat is geographically located within which massive salt marsh ecosystem?
questions.why: Chhari-Dhand is a seasonal desert wetland located in the Banni Grasslands of the Greater Rann of Kutch.

questions.q: Which Indian Ramsar site is historically the site of the world's first ever organized effort to ring (tag) birds for migratory research?
questions.why: Point Calimere in Tamil Nadu was the site where the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) pioneered bird ringing in India.

questions.q: The 'Shekha Jheel' Ramsar site in Uttar Pradesh was brought to international prominence by the ornithological efforts of which famous Indian birdman?
questions.why: The legendary ornithologist Dr. Salim Ali recognized Shekha Jheel's potential and actively campaigned for its early conservation.

questions.q: Which international organization provided the foundational scientific data identifying the 'Central Asian Flyway' used by birds visiting Indian Ramsar sites?
questions.why: Wetlands International, an official IOP of the Ramsar Convention, mapped the Central Asian Flyway crucial to Indian wetland conservation.

questions.q: As per recent constitutional environmental laws, the destruction of a designated Ramsar site in India can be prosecuted under the rules of which Act?
questions.why: The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, which govern Ramsar sites in India, are strictly notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

questions.q: The Patna Bird Sanctuary Ramsar site in Uttar Pradesh is historically famous for the seasonal congregation of which bird species?
questions.why: Patna Bird Sanctuary, despite its small size, supports massive congregations of wintering Rosy Pelicans and other waterfowl.

questions.q: Which is the only designated Ramsar site in India that is technically a 'meteorite crater'?
questions.why: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra is a highly alkaline and saline lake formed by a meteorite impact, making it globally unique among Ramsar sites.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of the 'National Wetland Decadal Change Atlas' published by ISRO?
opts: Tracking the spatial extent and loss of wetlands using satellites
questions.ansText: Tracking the spatial extent and loss of wetlands using satellites
questions.why: ISRO uses its Space Applications Centre to map and monitor the health and spatial changes of Indian wetlands via remote sensing.
